description: Two-moment cross-check of the Borromean/Brunnian Δ_λ magnitude identification (0-fit, from committed witnesses). Signs derived at both A (Milnor parity), but the same framing gives c₃/μ₃=0.63× and c₄/μ₄=0.0127× — inconsistent ~50×, with the A-trend backwards (clusters shrink O(h⁴)→O(h⁶) where the data grows). Downgrades the μ₃ near-miss toward coincidence; the magnitude identification fails the second moment. No fit; nothing wired.

data.verdict: TWO-MOMENT CROSS-CHECK FAILS — the Borromean/Brunnian magnitude identification does NOT survive the second moment (scope-(a), 0-fit). SIGNS derived at both A (Milnor parity (−1)^{A−1}: μ₃>0, μ₄<0). But the SAME framing gives f₃=c₃/μ₃=0.6308 (0.63×, the near-miss) and f₄=c₄/μ₄=0.01269 (~79× short) — INCONSISTENT by 49.72×. The A-trend is BACKWARDS: the physical residual moments GROW (|μ₄/μ₃|=9.752) while the Brunnian clusters SHRINK (|c₄/c₃|=0.1961), because the 4-link is O(h⁶) vs the 3-link's O(h⁴) — intrinsic topological suppression (first Milnor at length A ⇒ O(h^{2(A−1)})), un-tunable without a fit. CONCLUSION: this DOWNGRADES the μ₃ 0.63× 'near-miss' toward a coincidence — a framework matching one moment to 0.6× but the next to 0.01× with the A-trend inverted is not capturing the magnitude physics. The SIGN leg stands; the MAGNITUDE identification does not. No fit; μ_A never inverted; nothing wired.
